column2: Hearing his words, Vajra and the others said, "Let the fruit of good deeds be enjoyed first, and afterward that of sin."
Yama said again, "By the power of this man alone, go quickly to heaven, all of you, with your sons, friends and wives."
They mounted an excellent celestial car, attached to Dvijavarman, and, endowed with fitting rewards, went swiftly to heaven.
Dvijavarman, with his wife, passed beyond all the worlds, attained leadership of Shiva's hosts, and rejoices on Kailasa even today.
Indra said: O wise one, tell me the gradation of merit, and how the merit of building causeways and the like increases.
Brihaspati said: The illustrious Dvijavarman obtained half the fruit of the merit; Vajra obtained half of that, and the others shared the half of that.
An act is done in four ways, through mind, speech, body and effort; it is destroyed by the corresponding acts of expiation.
Indra said: What is the nature of liquor, what is its fault and what its merit? What food causes fault? Tell me this in detail.
Brihaspati said: Liquor from grain, from palm, from kaira, from madhuka flowers and from molasses — the sin decreases in that order, each by half.
For the three classes beginning with the kshatriyas liquor is said to be drinkable; for women too, the third kind and the rest may be drunk, except for brahmin women.
A widow, a maiden and a woman in her season should avoid it. A woman who greedily drinks liquor in her husband's absence
is called a madwoman; she should be shunned like an outcaste.
The penance for the twice-born is ten, eight, six and four; for women it is half that for liquor, and a quarter if in her husband's company.
A twice-born who drinks liquor out of delusion should perform the Krichchhra and Chandrayana penances and recite the Gayatri ten thousand times, or the Jataveda hymn.
Or he should recite the Ambika Hridaya and become pure. For the kshatriya and the other classes it is half and half again of that for the brahmin, in order;
for women the prescription is halved again, or it may be performed by brahmins on their behalf; or one may recite a thousand times standing in water and attain purity.
Lakshmi, Sarasvati, Gauri, Chandika, Tripurambika, Bhairava, Bhairavi, Kali, Mahashastri and the Mothers,
and other Shaktis — in their worship liquor is commended; but a brahmin versed in the Veda and its limbs should worship them without it.
Those who eat what has been offered to them, devoted solely to them and one with them, go with their current and, untainted, reach the supreme goal.
For all sins committed knowingly or unknowingly, this expiation is declared: remembering the feet of the supreme Shakti.
The base man who drinks liquor without worshipping the supreme Shakti dwells in the hell Raurava for as many years as there are drops.
The man who drinks liquor for pleasure is the lowest of men; there is no expiation for him other than falling from a rock or into fire.
A twice-born should not drink out of delusion, affection or desire. Through the grace of the great, through repentance for the deed,

through worship of the supreme Shakti, through restraints and observances, and through Chandrayana and Krichchhra penances performed for the stated number of days, a brahmin is purified; for a deliberate offence the penance is doubled.
Therefore desire is hard to overcome for all living beings. The creator of the universe, having made male and female forms, through desire itself
first set in motion activity consisting of creation, sustenance and dissolution. Through that activity they proceed; through its cessation they reach the imperishable goal.
How those who are wise may attain liberation through activity itself — hear now as I tell you that secret and that means.
Vasudeva, the all-self, is the ancient Person; this Lakshmi is the root Prakriti, mother of the whole world.
Union is performed for the satisfaction of the five and the non-five; if union is performed thus under the power of the mantra,
both of them act through the mantra, and no fault attaches to them.
This is for those strong in austerity; for others alone it leads downward. It applies only to one's own wife, and even for them it is by the force of the injunction.
For those two whose hearts are united as one self, whose minds are moist with devotion to the Goddess, there is no sin, unless on forbidden days.
This is Amba, mother of the world, and this Person is Sadashiva; for the satisfaction of the twenty-five principles union is now performed.
If union is performed under the power of this mantra, both are doers of merit, and no fault attaches to them.
And hear this, O lord of the gods, a supreme and great secret that destroys all sins at once.
Filled with devotion and faith, having bathed and standing in water, one should recite the fifteen-syllable mantra a thousand and eight times;
having worshipped the supreme Shakti, one is freed from all sins. By it are destroyed even sins done over crores of kalpas; one is freed from all calamities and obtains every wish.
Indra said: O Lord, knower of all dharma, devoted to the welfare of all beings, please explain the particulars of sin arising from association.
Brihaspati said: Sin arising from association is declared fourfold: the doer, the instigator, the helper and the one who consents, in order.
The sin decreases by a tenth in each case in turn; purification is by the method stated before.
Liquor, poisoned meat, exuded gums, mushrooms, a kind of onion, garlic, kalinga, the great kosha gourd,
bimbi, fungus, hastini, shishulambika, udumbara fig, brinjal, kataka and bilva-mallika —
the sin in eating these should be declared as decreasing tenfold in order. The seller of a city, a village, a vaishya's goods, or gifts to courtesans,
the servant, the city-dweller, the dweller in a bad village, the accused, the physician, the Vaikhanasa, the Shaiva, one who lives by women, the seller of food,
one who lives by arms, the wandering mendicant and the reviler of Vedic conduct — in eating the food of these, the sin decreases tenfold in order.
For food independently prepared with oil, the stated sin applies; for such food eaten after it has been seen by them, the stated sin should be declared.
For cooked rice of brahmins, kshatriyas, vaishyas and shudras, if one eats food cooked in oil that has not been seen, the sin is a quarter.
Food prepared by a twice-born man's maidservant — if seen by her, half of that; food of a courtesan is three quarters, likewise if seen.
The cowherd's food is like a shudra's, except for the four products of the cow; food cooked with oil, ghee and molasses from a vaishya is not defiled.
A fallen brahmin woman is like a vaishya; what is seen by her is somewhat defiled.
A twice-born who eats the food of a braggart should perform a hundred breath-controls, or recite the Drupada verse three times standing in water;
or he should likewise recite "Idam Vishnu" or the Tryambaka mantra in water, and fasting for one night, he is then purified of the sin.
Or he should sprinkle the food with the water-verses of the Pavamani hymns, recite the Anna Sukta and the Bhrigu Varuni passage,
and recite the verse "Brahmarpanam"; keeping the observance and fasting for one night, he will then become pure.
A woman who has eaten the food of such a person should feed one or more brahmins. In distress, a brahmin who eats their food incurs no fault.
Consecrating it seven times with the mantra "Idam Vishnu," meditating on it with the attitude "I am He," one who eats is not tainted by faults.
Or meditating on Shankara and reciting the Tryambaka mantra, with the attitude "I am He," through that knowledge one is not tainted by faults.
Hear my words, O lord of the gods, this secret: meditating on the supreme Goddess Shakti and reciting the fifteen-syllable mantra,
the twice-born who each day eats with the thought that it has been offered to her suffers nothing from the faults of food, nor fear of poverty,
nor fear of disease, nor fear of enemies; for the one who recites, there is liberation and auspiciousness everywhere and always.
Thus, O Shakra, I have told you in detail about sins and their expiations. What else do you wish to hear?

The nectar that arises when the milk ocean is churned — by drinking it you will become strong and immortal.
brahmandpuran:121:54	I will act so that the Daityas do not obtain any of this nectar and only suffer toil.
Thus instructed by Shri Vasudeva, all the gods then made a pact with the peerless Daityas. Gods and Asuras gathered herbs of many kinds,
cast them into the waters of the milk ocean, purer than the moon, made Mount Mandara the churning rod and Vasuki the rope, and began with effort to churn the lord of waters.
All the gods together were at the tail of Vasuki; the Daityas were placed at the head by Shauri.
Though strong, those Daityas, their bodies scorched by the fiery breath from his mouths, all lost their vigour.
The gods pulling at the tail were refreshed again and again by a favourable wind sent by Vishnu.
The glorious one, in the form of the primal Tortoise in the middle of the milk ocean, became the support of the whirling Mandara mountain.
In another form Madhava pulled Vasuki with force among all the gods, and in yet another among the Daityas.
In the form of Brahma he held the mountain that pressed upon the ocean; and in another, O divine sage, with great splendour again and again
he strengthened the gods, by which they grew mighty; and with another splendour, able to bear the strain,
Janardana, possessor of all powers, strengthened the serpent. Then, as the milk ocean was being churned by gods and Danavas,
Surabhi, worshipped by the gods, appeared before them. Then gods and Daityas rejoiced, O ascetic.
As the milk ocean was churned again by gods and Danavas, while the perfected ones in heaven wondered, "What is this?"
the goddess Varuni arose, her eyes rolling with intoxication; smiling, she stood before the Asuras.
The Daityas did not take her, and so they became Asuras; because they have no sura (liquor), they are called Asuras.
Then she stood before all the gods; prompted by the Supreme One, the gods joyfully took her, and because they took sura they are called Suras.
As the churning went on, the great tree Parijata appeared, perfuming the world all around with its fragrance.
Troops of Apsarases of exceedingly beautiful form and composure appeared, O divine sage, enchanting all the worlds.
Then the cool-rayed moon arose, and Maheshvara took it; the poison that arose was taken by the serpent races.
Then Janardana took the jewel called Kaustubha. Then arose the great herb named Vijaya, intoxicating with the scent of its leaves; Bhairava took it.
Then the god Dhanvantari himself appeared, wearing divine garments and holding in his hand a water-pot full of nectar.
Then the gods and Daityas everywhere were glad at heart, and the sages too were satisfied, O treasury of austerity.
Then from that great milk ocean arose Shri, dwelling in the blooming lotus, the giver of boons, lotus in hand.
Then all the sages, glad at heart, praised the supreme Shri with the Shri Sukta, and the Gandharvas sang exquisitely.
All the troops of Apsarases led by Vishvachi danced, and the holy rivers beginning with the Ganga came to bathe her.
The eight elephants of the quarters took water in sacred vessels and bathed that Shri who dwells in the lotus.
Tulasi also arose, precious and born of union with Hari; the embodied milk ocean gave her a garland of lotuses.
Vishvakarman offered her divine ornaments. Wearing divine garlands and garments and adorned with divine ornaments, Rama went to the breast of Vishnu as all looked on.
Tulasi was worn by the mighty Vishnu. And the goddess who dwells on Vishnu's breast, great queen of all the worlds, looked upon the gods with a glance moist with compassion.
Her chin was round like a mirror, her lips rosy; with rows of bright, pure teeth, radiant like forms of knowledge,
shining like jasmine buds, her teeth displayed moonlight; she was radiant with a nose-ornament set with large pearls;
her eyes were long, like the hollow of an inner ketaka petal; her forehead was like the half-moon, with locks well arranged;
her ears were adorned with ruby earrings; her betel was fragrant with fresh camphor and musk;
her face was sweet like the orb of the lovely autumn moon; she had a gleaming musk mark and a mass of dark curls;
she shone with a line of vermilion placed in the parting of her hair;
crowned with a shining crescent moon, her eyes rolling with intoxication, rich in every charming attire and adorned with every ornament.
Seeing her playing with a ball, her ornaments swaying, the Lord quickly left Uma and ran after her.
Uma too, seeing her beloved running, deeply astonished and reproaching herself and her own beauty, stood silent with downcast face, filled with shame and jealousy.
Somehow seizing her, he embraced her again and again; she, shaking him off repeatedly, ran far away.
Seizing her again, the Lord, overcome by desire, embraced her with great force, and then his seed was released.
From it arose the god Mahashasta of great strength, capable of quenching the pride of many crores of Daitya lords.
By the touch of the drops of that seed, the ground here and there took on the colour of silver and gold, O subduer of the Vindhya.
Likewise that goddess who bewitches the world vanished, and Girisha, having turned back, went to the mountain with Gauri as companion.
Now I shall tell you this wonder, O husband of Lopamudra; listen. It has been told to no one and rests only in my heart.
Long ago there was one named Bhandasura, crest-jewel of all the Daityas, skilful, who at will ruled over the gods of many kinds.
From his right shoulder he created a Daitya named Vishukra, able to protect his party, equal to Shukra in judgment.
From his left shoulder the Danava Bhanda created Vishanga, the chief of the wicked, and a sister named Dhumini.
With his two brothers of fierce valour, having slain his foes, exalted in heroism and might, he shattered the cosmic egg.
Brahma, Vishnu and Maheshvara, seeing him blazing with splendour, at once took to flight and stayed in their own abodes.
At that very moment, crushed by his arms and fainting, the hosts of the heavenly ones could not even breathe.
Some in the depths of Patala, some in the waters of the ocean, some in the corners of the quarters, some in mountain thickets —
they hid, greatly terrified, abandoning wives, sons and women; the gods, fallen from their offices, wandered about in disguise.
Regarding the Yakshas, great serpents, Siddhas, Sadhyas proud in battle, Brahma, the lotus-naveled one, Rudra and the wielder of the thunderbolt — all the worlds — as mere straw, Bhanda ruled.
Then, to slay Bhandasura and to protect the three worlds, a third form arose from the fire of the great sacrifice, O sage.
They call the one who bears that form Lalita, the supreme deity, whose four arms are adorned with noose, goad, bow and arrows.
That goddess, the supreme Shakti, whose nature is the supreme Brahman, skilled in war, slew the Daitya lord Bhanda in battle.
Chitrakarman, full of joy, embraced him with both arms and said, "Praise Mahadeva, child; he grants the accomplishment of every aim."
Saying this, the one of boundless intellect taught him the Shatarudriya; reciting the Shatarudriya, he bowed to Rudra a hundred times.
Then the Lord Mahadeva, whose banner is the bull, being pleased, offered him a boon, and the boy chose this boon:
Whatever strength my opponent employs against my strength, let his chief missiles and weapons prove useless against me.
Promising "So be it," the Lord, after some reflection, also gave him a kingdom for sixty thousand years.
Seeing this deed, the Creator said "Bhandi, bhandi!" and therefore he is known in the worlds by the name Bhanda.
Having given him the boon, and missiles and weapons as well, he, surrounded by all the hosts of sages, vanished right there.
Hari always slays all of your race simply by birth. The illusion by which you are deluded was created by him.
Seeing you deluded and seeking a weak point, Indra is performing great austerities to gain victory over you.
If the Mother of the world is pleased, victory will be his. Abandon this illusory world, go with your ministers to the Himalaya mountain, and obstruct your enemies.
Thus addressed by his preceptor, he left his splendid couch, summoned his elder ministers, and told them what had happened.
Hearing this and reflecting, Shrutavarman said to the king, "A kingdom of sixty thousand years was granted to you by Shiva.
More than that has passed many times over, O hero. What is impelled by time and Shiva cannot be countered.
It cannot be countered except by worshipping him. In due time one must experience both sorrow and joy."
Then the one named Bhimakarman said, "An enemy should not be ignored, according to one's strength. If we obstruct his rites, victory will be yours.
In battle, O great king, Shiva himself gave you the knowledge that takes away the strength of others; therefore victory is always yours."
Bhanda, lord of the Danavas, approved his words; setting out with his armies, he went to the slopes of the Himalaya.
Seeing the Danavas intent on obstructing the austerities, the Mother of the world raised before them a great, shining, impassable rampart.
Seeing it, the Danava lord, astonished and wondering what it was, grew enraged and broke it with a Danava missile of great power.
Again it stood before him, impassable for all the Danavas; the bold one broke it with the wind missile and roared.
Again and again, though reduced to ashes, it reappeared. Seeing this, the Daitya lord returned dejected to his city.
Seeing that Mother of the world and the shining rampart, the gods trembled with fear and abandoned all their rites.
Then Shakra said to them, "This Daitya lord has come here; he cannot be fought in battle even by all of us together.
Even if we flee, we have no other refuge anywhere. Let us properly make a beautiful fire-pit a yojana wide,
establish the fire by the rite of the great sacrifice, and worship the supreme Shakti, we gods, with great offerings of our own flesh.
We shall either become one with Brahman or enjoy heaven." Thus addressed, all those gods led by Indra
duly offered oblations, cutting off their flesh piece by piece with mantras. When all the flesh had been offered, and the feet and hands,
as the gods were about to offer their entire bodies, a supreme, unsurpassed mass of splendour appeared.
From its midst arose an unsurpassed wheel-shaped form; and in its centre the great Goddess, radiant as the rising sun,
reviver of the world, whose self is Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, the very limit of the essence of beauty, an ocean of the nectar of bliss,
like the hibiscus flower, clad in garments like pomegranate blossoms, wearing every ornament, the sole abode of the sentiment of love,
whose glances from the corners of her eyes spread moonlight in waves of compassion, her hands resplendent with noose, goad, sugarcane bow and five arrows.
Beholding that great Goddess, all the gods with Vasava, glad at heart, bowed again and again to her who is the self of all.
Looked upon by her, they were at once free from pain, whole in limb, very firm, with bodies like diamond and of great strength; and they praised the great Goddess Ambika, giver of every aim.

Be gracious, O Mistress of the universe, adored by the universe; be gracious, O Mistress of knowledge whose form is the Veda; be gracious, O you who consist of maya and are embodied in mantra; be gracious, O Mistress of all, whose form is everything.
Having thus praised the great Goddess, all the gods with Vasava bowed again and again and swiftly took refuge in her.
Then the Goddess, pleased, seeing Vasava bowing, the giver of boons to all embodied beings offered him a boon.
Indra said: If you are pleased, O auspicious one, grant me life, which is hard to bear, oppressed as I am by the Daitya lord; we have come to you seeking refuge.
The Goddess said: I myself will conquer Bhanda, born of the Daitya race, and soon give you the three worlds with all that moves and does not move.
Let all the hosts of gods be fearless and joyful. Those men who praise me with devotion by this hymn
will always be vessels of dharma, prosperity and fame, endowed with learning and humility, free from disease and long-lived,
rich in sons, friends and wives by my grace. Having thus received the boon, the gods and the mighty lord of the gods
attained supreme delight, gazing at her again and again.
Beautiful houses for the vassals, ministers, soldiers and brahmins, and for the Vetalas, servants and maidservants;
in the middle a divine royal palace adorned with gates and gate-towers, with many halls and beautiful assembly rooms;
and a lovely throne-hall made of the nine gems, and in its centre a divine throne made of the wish-granting gem,
self-luminous, peerless, like the rising sun. Seeing it, Brahma, grandsire of the worlds, reflected:

Whoever sits upon this, even a fool, will by the power of this city surpass all the worlds.
brahmandpuran:126:15	A woman alone is not fit to rule, nor a man without her. The scripture says one should consecrate one bearing the marks of a great person, attended by auspicious rites, together with a suitable consort.
brahmandpuran:126:16	This lady of fine hips shines as the embodied goddess of love. In the three worlds there is no bridegroom for her other than Shankara.
brahmandpuran:126:17	But he has matted hair, wears skulls, has deformed eyes and carries a skull-bowl, is spotted, smeared with ashes and adorned with bones from the cremation ground —
brahmandpuran:126:18	how could she, the most auspicious, choose this abode of the inauspicious? As Brahma was thinking thus, Maheshvara,
possessing the beauty of a crore of Kandarpas, with a divine body, wearing divine garments and a garland, anointed with divine perfumes,
adorned with crown, necklace, armlets, earrings and the like, appeared before him in a form that enchants the world.
Embracing that youth, Brahma, grandsire of the worlds, named him Kameshvara, bearer of a lovely form.
This is a bridegroom worthy of that supreme Shakti. Having decided thus, they went with him to her.
Brahma, Vishnu and Maheshvara praised the supreme Shakti. Seeing her with the eyes of a young doe, the youthful blue-red god was seized by love and forgot all his rites.
She too, the slender one, seeing him like Love embodied, her whole body overcome by desire, regarded him as her own self. Both, intent on gazing at each other, were stricken by love,
knowing every nuance of feeling, steadfast and high-minded, their conduct unknown to others, their minds unsettled for a moment.
Then Brahma said to the great Goddess, sole mistress of the worlds: "These gods and sages and hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases wish to see you, the Queen, with your beloved in the great battle.
Who, O Goddess, is a suitable beloved for you, the most blessed of men? For the protection of the worlds, accept the supreme Person.
Be queen of this city; sit upon the excellent throne. We wish to see you consecrated by the illustrious, sinless divine sages,
bearing the emblems of sovereignty and wearing every ornament, seated on the throne with your beloved."
Accepting the waving of lights performed by the Apsarases, she descended from the top of the celestial car and entered the great hall.
Sitting on the throne with the god Shambhu, the omniscient one, by a mere glance, fulfilled whatever the great people there desired in their minds.
Seeing this deed of the Goddess, Brahma, grandsire of the worlds, then gave her the names Kamakshi and Kameshvari.
At her command a cloud of wonders rained upon that city costly things and divine ornaments.
The wish-granting gem, the wish-fulfilling tree, Kamala and the wish-granting cows then stood in every house, before the Goddess, for victory.
Wholly devoted to her service, freed from other activities and qualities, endowed with all desires and aims, they rejoiced at all times.
The Grandsire, Hari, Mahadeva and Vasava, the other lords of the quarters and all the hosts of gods,
the divine sages led by Narada, the yogins led by Sanaka, the great sages led by Manu, and the ascetics led by Vasishtha,
Gandharvas, Apsarases, Yakshas and other divine races who dwell crowded in heaven, on earth and in the atmosphere —
all of them dwelt without crowding in that city.
Thus the Goddess, affectionate to them, not going elsewhere, constantly pleased all the people with great love.
As queen of the king on the great earth, she yielded the desires of all who dwell on the earth, fulfilling every wish of the wise.
While Kama-Shankara with Amba was the sole ruler of the three worlds, ten thousand years passed like a single moment.
Then one day the divine sage Narada came, bowed to the supreme Shakti and spoke humbly:

Supreme Brahman, supreme abode, the purifier, O supreme Mistress, whose nature comprises the true and untrue, resolve and doubt,
brahmandpuran:127:48	you have taken manifest form for the prosperity of the world, to destroy the wicked and uplift the good; your activity, O auspicious one, is for the protection of the virtuous.
brahmandpuran:127:49	This Asura Bhanda, O Goddess, torments the three worlds. He must be conquered by you alone; the other gods cannot do it.
brahmandpuran:127:50	The gods, devoted solely to your service, have dwelt here a long time; at your command they will go to their own cities,
brahmandpuran:127:51	which are inauspicious and empty; may they become prosperous through you. Thus requested by Narada, the Mistress of all sent the immortals to dwell in their own abodes.
Having honoured Brahma, Hari, Shambhu, Vasava and the other lords of the quarters as befitted them, Ambika sent them away.
The gods, though sent away, so as not to incur offence, served Shiva and Shiva, the primal parents, through their own portions.
This account of the appearance of the great Goddess and her coronation gives long life and is the cause of all auspiciousness.
The wise one who rises at dawn and recites it with devotion and faith becomes rich in wealth, and his speech becomes like nectar.
No misfortune befalls that wise one here or hereafter; he obtains vast fame and pre-eminence among his peers.
His prosperity becomes steady and he meets with good at every step; he never knows fear and becomes radiant and mighty.
Free from the threefold suffering, he is filled with the aims of life. The best of reciters who recites it daily at the three junctions, meditating on the Queen of the throne,
attains great prosperity within six months.
Then, as the Mantranatha, the Sanketa Yogini, set foot in motion, a kahali horn announcing the departure sounded in the sky.
The army of Shaktis marched out, adorned in charming attire, dark and lustrous like the leopard, holding lutes in their hands.
Some sang and danced, with voices like intoxicated cuckoos, playing lute, flute, drum and the like, stepping gracefully.
The dark Shaktis moved on, delighting the people of the world; some rode peacocks, some swans,
some mongooses, some sat upon cuckoos; all were dark in form; some stood in eared chariots;
some, intoxicated with kadamba wine, rode horses; placing the Mantranatha in front, they marched on and on.
Then, mounting a great chariot with lofty banner and wheels, wearing armour the colour of the morning sun, her eyes rolling with intoxication,
her lotus face charming with slight drops of sweat, surveying with floods of sidelong glances and the dance of her curving brows
the whole of that exceedingly proud army of Shaktis, with a great insignia and an umbrella of three peacock feathers,
in the midst of them, with a brilliance unlike the other Shaktis, went forth the Shyamala, dark as a rain-cloud, the leader of mantras.
The dwellers of heaven praised her with sixteen names; hear those sixteen names, O pot-born one:
Sangitayogini, Shyama, Shyamala, Mantranayika, Mantrini, Sachiveshi, Pradhaneshi, Shukapriya,
Vinavati, Vainiki, Mudrini, Priyakapriya, Nipapriya, Kadambeshi, Kadambavanavasini
and Sadamada — these are the sixteen names, O pot-born one. Whoever, embodied, praises the Queen of ministers even once with these, the whole of the three worlds rests in his hand, without doubt.
Wherever that Mantrinatha casts her glance, there the enemy army falls utterly, without doubt.
Whatever discussion there is of the rule of the supreme Queen Lalita, and whatever discussion of the Shaktis, it grants victory everywhere.
Then from the parrot in the hand of the Sangitayogini came forth the Dhanurveda, bearing a strung bow,
a four-armed hero, three-headed and three-eyed. Bowing to the chief Queen, the devoted one said this:

O Goddess, you are setting out for battle with the Asura lord Bhanda; therefore I must render you help, O leader of ministers.
brahmandpuran:129:41	Take this very great bow named Chitrajiva, O Mother of the worlds, destroyer of Danavas.
brahmandpuran:129:42	And take these two gold-painted quivers filled with inexhaustible arrows, for the destruction of the Daityas and as a sign of favour to me.
Thus bowing his head, the Dhanurveda offered them with devotion, and Priyakapriya took the bow and quivers.
Taking the great bow Chitrajiva, Shukapriya made it resound, twanging the bowstring many times.
The Sangitayogini filled the world with the sound of the bow, to the rich delight of the minds and eyes of the heaven-dwellers.
She had two attendants, one of them Yantrini; carrying the parrot and the lute, they attended her.
The dark one, holding the bow whose string's sound grew with the jingling of her swaying bracelets, made it exceedingly charming.
Adorned with the bow Chitrajiva, the Gitayogini shone like a bank of clouds, her bow like an umbrella of kadamba.
The arrow gleaming in her right hand sparkled, sharp as Kali's glance and fearsome as a dancing serpent.
Behind her, riding a chariot marked with the wheel of song, attended goddesses of equal dark beauty, bearing bows and arrows,
numbering a thousand akshauhinis, swift and languid with intoxication, filling the quarters with sweet "kilikila" cries.
Resplendent with a white umbrella ten yojanas wide, made of clear pearls, covering the three worlds and rivalling the orb of the moon;
fanned by hosts of attendants led by Vijaya, shining with jewels, and by four chowries as lovely as waves of new moonlight;
proclaiming the rank of sole sovereign of the Shaktis, her army adorned with hundreds of emblems of empire, her glory praised by the music and song of the celestial women, of clear radiance —
beyond the reach of speech and beyond the reach of intellect, not to be conceived as such, incomparable —

touching the pride of the imperial wealth of the circle of Shaktis that fills the womb of the three worlds, served from nearby by those vying to be first, with palms joined on their heads in fervent devotion;
glancing at the faces of Brahma, Ishvara, Vishnu, Vrisha and the foremost gods pouring out praises; suddenly bearing the three worlds made of light that arose from her blazing five flower-arrows;
showered with victorious and auspicious parched grain by troops of Apsarases radiant as lightning, and by the lovely goddesses beginning with Kameshvari, charming in their battle attire,
whose blazing weapons outshone the sun — attended at her feet by the Nitya goddesses; driving the chariot Shrichakra, marked with the tilaka, whose banner ten yojanas high scraped the clouds,
joined with ranks of fierce and mighty Shaktis, driving her chariot into battle, clad in spotless garments of rising tawny hue, she shone charmingly in the battle.
Praised by the gods with twenty-five jewel-like names, exceedingly able to allay the sins of the world, Lalita set out for battle.
Agastya said: O horse-faced one of great intellect, give me the twenty-five names of Lalita, the supreme Queen, a nectar for the ears.
Hayagriva said: Simhasana, Shri Lalita, Maharajni, Parankusha, Chapini, Tripura, Mahatripurasundari,
Sundari, Chakranatha, Samrajni, Chakrini, Chakreshvari, Mahadevi, Kameshi, Parameshvari,
Kamarajapriya, Kamakotiga, Chakravartini, Mahavidya, Shivanangavallabha, Sarvapatala,
Kulanatha, Amnayanatha, Sarvamnayanivasini and Shringaranayika — with these twenty-five names
those who praise the illustrious Lalita, the supreme Queen, obtain good fortune, the eight perfections and great fame.
Thus, driving her great army with fierce eagerness, Lalitambika, enraged, advanced against Bhandasura.
Hear from me the names of those called the Guptas, mentioned before, who stand on the red chariot to destroy Bhandasura:
Kamakarshanika, Buddhyakarshanika Kala, Ahankarakarshini, Shabdakarshanika Kala,
Sparshakarshanika Nitya, Rupakarshanika Kala, Rasakarshanika Nitya, Gandhakarshanika Kala,
Chittakarshanika Nitya, Dhairyakarshanika Kala, Smrityakarshanika Nitya, Namakarshanika Kala,
Bijakarshanika Nitya, Atmakarshanika Kala, Amritakarshani Nitya and Sharirakarshini Kala.
These sixteen Shaktis, in the form of the digits of the moon, occupying the eighth tier, are known by the name Gupta.
Like coral trees, charming with gentle smiles, four-armed and three-eyed, bright with crowns of moon and sun,
bearing bow and arrows, shield and sword, of divine radiance, they set out to slay Bhandasura, O pot-born one.
In the seventh tier of the chariot, bright as a lamp blazing at dusk, dwell those called the Guptataras:
Anangamadana with Anangamadanatura, Anangalekha, Anangavega and Anangankusha,
and Anangamalini — these goddesses, the colour of hibiscus, bearing sugarcane bow, flower arrows, flower ball and lotus,
endowed with great valour, at Lalita's command stand as if blazing with anger against Bhandasura.
Then in the sixth tier of the king of chariots stand those led by Sarvasankshobhini, known as the Sampradayas,
their masses of hair braided, bright with vermilion marks, of exceedingly fierce nature, radiant like the fire of doom,
bearing fire-arrows, fire-bows, fire-swords and fire-shields called Vahnichakra, with blazing bodies,
enraged against the Asura lord, born from the ashes of Kama — these are the command-Shaktis of the mighty Lalita:
Sarvasankshobhini, Sarvavidravini, the Shakti Sarvakarshanika, Sarvahladinika,
the Shakti Sarvasammohini, the Shakti Sarvastambhana, the Shakti Sarvajrimbhana, the Shakti Sarvonmadana,
the Shakti Sarvarthasadhika, Sarvasampattipurani, the Shakti Sarvamantramayi and Sarvadvandvakshayankari.
Thus the names of the Sampradayas have been told. Now those in the fifth tier are remembered as the Kulottirnas.
They are like crystal, bearing axe, noose, mace, bell and gem, with blazing bodies,
exceedingly angry with the enemy of the gods, their faces crooked with frowns. Hear their names too, O pot-born one:
the goddess Sarvasiddhiprada, Sarvasampatprada, the goddess Sarvapriyankari, Sarvamangalakarini,
the goddess Sarvakamaprada, Sarvaduhkhavimochini,
Sarvamrityuprashamini, Sarvavighnanivarini, the goddess Sarvangasundari and Sarvasaubhagyadayini.
These ten goddesses have been named, their hearts filled with compassion. In the fourth tier of the chariot, radiant like pearl necklaces,
are the ten known by the name Nigarbha Yoginis: Sarvajna, Sarvashakti, Sarvaishvaryaprada,
the goddess Sarvajnanamayi, Sarvavyadhivinashini, Sarvadharasvarupa, Sarvapapahara,
the goddess Sarvanandamayi, Sarvarakshasvarupini, and the tenth deity, to be known as Sarvepsitaphalaprada.
These should be known as four-armed, bearing thunderbolt, spear, lance and discus, intent on slaying Bhandasura.
Then in the third tier of the king of chariots are the famous Rahasya Yoginis, the mistresses of speech,
like red ashoka blossoms, with arrows and bows in hand, their bodies wholly covered in armour, adorned with lute and book:
Vashini, Kameshi, Bhogini, Vimala, Aruna, the one called Jayini, Sarveshi and Kaulini.
These eight goddesses are remembered as causes of the destruction of the Daityas. Then in the second tier of the king of chariots
are three, dwelling in the three seats, eight-armed, bearing bow and arrows, drinking vessel, citron and small sword,
shield, serpent-noose and a bell of great sound, intoxicated with wine, most secret and hidden:
Kameshi, Vajreshi and the other, Bhagamalini — these three goddesses are remembered as filled with anger against Bhanda.
Equal to Lalita in greatness and equal to Lalita in splendour, these are declared the ever-intimate companions of the Goddess.
Then on the great seat of bliss in the middle tier of the chariot, dwelling all around, are those of the fifteen syllables,
the Tithi Nityas, whose form is time, pervading the universe, their brows knitted in anger against Bhandasura and the other Daityas,
like the Goddess in form and in weapons, present age after age for the benefit of the worlds.
Learn their names from me, O pot-born one: Kameshi, Bhagamala, Nityaklinna,
Bherunda, Vahnivasini, Mahavajreshvari, Duti, the goddess Tvarita, the ninth Kulasundari,
Nitya, Nilapataka, Vijaya, Sarvamangala, Jvalamalinika and Chitra — fifteen are declared.
With these, ever intent solely on her service, the supreme Queen went forth to conquer the wicked Bhandasura.
